Egy egyszerű, 90 napos keret, amivel a n: A simple 90-day framework for building a social media presence from scratch that brings in clients — not just followers.
A közösségi média a legolcsóbb módja ann: Social media is the cheapest way to make a brand visible — and the fastest way to waste your time if you don't have a plan. Here's a simple 90-day framework, starting from nothing.
Előbb: a lájk nem cél: First things first: likes aren't the goal
A követőszám és a lájk hiúsági mutató. A: Follower counts and likes are vanity metrics. The real goal is attention, trust, and finally an enquiry that buys. Measure every decision against that — not against whether the number looks nice.
Organikus vagy fizetett? Nem ugyanaz a f: Organic or paid? They're not the same job
Mielőtt bármit elkezdesz, érdemes külön: Before you start anything, it's worth keeping the two apart, because their timescales are completely different:
<strong>Organikus közösségépítés</strong: Organic community building — measured in months. It builds recognition and trust, which then supports every other channel. That's what this article is about.
<strong>Fizetett ügyfélszerzés</strong>: Paid client acquisition — measured in campaign cycles, typically 30 days. If you need enquiries now, this is the faster route: this is how we win clients.
A kettő nem helyettesíti egymást. A hird: Neither replaces the other. Advertising brings the enquiry; your organic presence decides what someone finds when they look you up — which is exactly why it's fine that community building is slower.
<strong>Válassz 1–2 platformot,</strong>: Pick 1–2 platforms, where your audience actually is. Better to stand out on one than to be half-present on five.
<strong>Rakd rendbe a profilt:</strong>: Sort out the profile: a clear name, picture and bio that says in one sentence who you help and with what, plus a contact detail or link.
<strong>Határozd meg a hangnemet:</stron: Define the tone: how does your brand speak? It shows up in everything, from posts to replies.
<strong>Nézd meg a versenytársakat:</str: Look at the competition: what works for them and what doesn't — don't copy it, learn from it.
<strong>Építs 3–4 tartalompillért:</stro: Build 3–4 content pillars: for example education (tips), trust (case studies, behind the scenes), product/service, and personality. That way you won't run out of ideas.
<strong>Legyen ütemterved:</strong> inká: Have a schedule: three good posts a week you can sustain beats one a day that runs out after a fortnight.
<strong>Rövid videó viszi a szót:</stron: Short video leads the way: organic reach on Reels/TikTok/Shorts is the strongest right now. You don't need a professional studio — you need a clear message and a good first 2 seconds.
<strong>Kezeld a közösséget:</strong> vá: Manage the community: reply to comments and messages. Both the algorithm and people reward genuine interaction.
<strong>Nézd meg, mi működött:</strong>: Look at what worked: which topic, format and post brought saves, shares and messages. Do more of that.
<strong>Told meg fizetéssel a nyerteseke: Boost the winners with money — but only after tracking is in place: get conversion tracking working first, or you're just buying reach. (More on this: what Google Ads costs.) Then it's worth amplifying the best-performing organic post — not advertising at random.
<strong>Vezess egy egyszerű riportot:</s: Keep a simple report: reach, engagement and — what actually matters — how many enquiries or messages came in. That last one is the only number you should move budget on; the rest is just signal.
Minden platformra ugyanaz a tartalom, vá: The same content on every platform, unchanged.
Csak eladni akarsz — érték nélkül. Ököls: Only selling, with no value given. As a rule of thumb an 80% value / 20% offer ratio tends to work — that's experience, not a measured result.
Giving up after two weeks because “it isn't working”. Community building is measured in months, not days.
Kevés platform, világos hangnem, tarthat: Few platforms, a clear tone, a sustainable rhythm, and measurement at the end — that's the difference between “we post things” and “social media brings us clients”. If you'd rather not run it yourself: this is how we handle social media.
